en:
Subspace warp drive
disengaged. We will soon
be arriving in destination
planet's orbit.

Approximately 40 percent
of the surface is covered
by land, and only 30
percent is not obstructed
by canopy. There are no
cities with populations
exceeding 100,000.

Internal combustion
engines have yet to be
invented here. Civilization
is likely still in its early
stages.

As we have no data on
this star system, I have
randomly assigned this
planet the name <font color=yellow>Maere</font>.
Maere...?
Ah, good. Your vitals are\nback to normal. You\nappear to be doing better.
E.V.E.L.Y.S.S.E. is your\nname, correct?
You can call me Eve. It is\ngood to properly meet―
What is wrong!? Are you\nfeeling ill?
Your face unsettled me, is\nall! I'll be fine so long as\nyou stay away from me!

How rude! I will have you
know my appearance was
calculated specifically to
be endearing to humans!
Ahem. Moving on, I have\nreregistered your name as\nE.V.E. in my system.

I am glad to see you are
doing better. We were
quite worried about your
condition.

Like I said, I am perfectly
fine. So long as you have
the need and gems, I can
summon an ally whenever
you wish!
There is just one thing...
So you have lost all of\nyour memories?
Yes. It is as though a\nheavy fog has obscured\nparts of my mind...

While I can still recall my
name, no matter how hard
I try, I am unable to
remember how I learned
that spell or why I was on
that planet...

Never fear, never fear!
You can travel with us
until you regain your
memories.
After all, companions on\nthe road lighten your\nfighting load!
I would like that. Thank\nyou.

I am confident that by
accompanying you, I will
be able to recall all that I
have forgotten.

Added to that, you will no
doubt find me to be a
valuable ally! My
symbology is nothing to
scoff at!
Now enough about me!\nHow is the ship?
Ah, right...
Well, our shields failing has\nhad quite a negative\neffect on the ship's flight.

Space dust, though
normally negligible, now
does a great deal of
damage when we travel at
high speeds.
Unfortunately, until we\nobtain replacement parts,\nI cannot make any repairs.

If we were, however, able
to harness enough energy,
we might be able to erect
a shield strong enough to
repel the dust.

Very well. Then let us
descend upon this planet
and see if we can locate a
source of energy.

Exploring an unknown
planet... How exciting! I'd
like to join you in your
search, if you don't mind!

In that case, it falls to me
to look after the ship
while the two of you are
away! I will not let you
down!
Now let us commence the\nlanding process.
Huh...!? Oh, dear...!
Captain, we have an\nemergency!
Something has gone\nterribly wrong, but I\ncannot identify what!
Mayhap it is you that is\nmalfunctioning?
I am operating quite\nnormally, thank you!

The same, however,
cannot be said for the
rest of the ship. Upon
entering Maere's
atmosphere, the
short-range sensors quit
responding.
All systems remain intact.\nThe cause of this failure is\nstill uncertain...
Sounds to me like the\nproblem lies with the AI\nitself.

This is far from ideal. How
are we to locate the
materials we need if our
sensors aren't working?
I suppose you would have\nto go outside and conduct\nan unassisted search.

So you're asking the
captain to aimlessly
wander about an unknown
planet until we find what
we've come here for!?
What you suggest is
incredibly reckless!
I am sorry. You are right.\nIt was a terrible idea.
Yes, but let us not get\nahead of ourselves just\nyet!
According to the\nfederation manual...

In situations like this, we
must first secure our
landing site against any
potential threats.
Seeing as our sensors are\ndown, you will have to rely\non your own instincts.
My summoned companion\nand I will accompany you\noutside, Captain.

In the meantime, I shall
run a diagnostic to
determine if the sensors
are our only problem.
Godspeed, my friends.\nStay safe.
Good work! All the\ndangerous beasts lurking\nnearby are dead, I take it?

I also did my part! With
some help from this handy
federation manual, I kept
the ship safe in your
absence!

Yes, thanks to the
captain, our operation
went smoothly. Did you
finish analyzing the ship?
I am so glad you asked!\nYou will not believe what I\ndiscovered!
The sensors are, in fact,\nfunctioning properly!
What is the problem,\nthen?

It seems this planet is
emitting some sort of
waves that prevent the
sensors' signals from
transmitting properly.

I agree that it is odd an
underdeveloped civilization
should be in possession of
such technologies.
If you are aware of the\ncause, why haven't you\nfixed the issue yet?

Well, to do that, we would
need to track down the
source of this interference
and destroy it.

...Only, the very sensors
that would be able to
locate said source are
down.
*Sigh* We are going in\ncircles here.
Interfering with the\ninterference...? A brilliant\nidea, Captain!

So we should create an
interference system that
will generate interference,
which interferes with the
interference waves that
are interfering with―
Are you trying to confuse\nus on purpose?
...I thought I was being\nfunny.

Ahem. What I was trying
to say is we can create a
jammer that will block out
the waves obstructing our
sensors.

If we carry it some
distance from the ship,
the sensors should be
able to see everything
located between them and
our device!

So the further away from
the ship we take it, the
more our sensors will be
able to view?

Correct. Then, when we
pinpoint the cause of our
trouble, we can attach our
<font color=yellow>counter-jammer</font> to it.
The more ground you\ncover, the better our\nsensors will work.

While I am under no
illusions this will be easy, I
do believe it will be worth
the effort.
May I get started on\ncreating the device?

Thank you. It should be
ready by the time you
embark upon your
scouting mission.

I will take care of the
counter-jammer. The
captain will be needing
both hands to take down
any obstacles we face
along the way.
Ah, teamwork at its finest!
Now that we have a clear\nplan of action, I am feeling\nrather relieved!
It's too early to relax. The\nhard part starts now.
I am sure it is nothing the\ntwo of you cannot handle.\nRight, Captain?

Thanks to your efforts, I
was able to map a route
from our ship to Maere's
sea.

Though I do not know
what the ocean here is
comprised of, I suspect it
can be broken down into
deionized water and a
number of minerals.
The good news is, these\nresources will likely prove\nto be very valuable!

The bad news is,
procuring them will not be
easy. There appear to be
sinister entities lurking
along the coastline...

I-it gets worse... I suspect
they are not exactly the
kind that are alive. They
are gh-gh-ghosts, if you
will.
You, of all people, should\nnot fear ghosts.

What is that supposed to
mean? Are you trying to
imply that my face can
even frighten away the
dead!?
Not at all.
R-regardless of what you\nhave to say, I am quite\ncontent with how I look!

You need not sulk. There
is nothing wrong with your
face. I simply found it
amusing that you, a robot,
are afraid of ghosts.
...There is nothing wrong\nwith my face? Do you\nreally mean that?
Of course.
Hehehe! I knew you people\nsecretly found me\ncharming!
...Well, that was easy.
What was that?

N-nothing! Just that the
captain and I must depart
posthaste. There isn't a
minute to spare!
Come now, <player>!
Be careful, you two!\nGh-gh-ghosts are not to\nbe taken lightly!

Excellent work, everyone!
We have successfully
secured ourselves a
source of salt water!

This will afford us
drinkable water, oxygen,
and even some natural
salt that can be used for
cooking, should you feel
like it!
Natural salt... That sounds\nwonderful.
Captain, what is wrong?\nWhy do you look so\nsomber?
You want to know more\nabout the last enemy you\nfought?

According to the
Quadscanner, the creature
has the same genetic
composition as the other
creatures on this planet.
Glowing spikes protruding\nfrom their body?

The scanner is unable to
provide me with details
regarding that, but they
are clearly visible in the
sample shot provided.
Is everything all right,\nEve? You appear to be\nsweating.
Are your memories\nreturning to you?
Are you feeling sick\nagain?
You must be the type that\nsweats a lot.
No... It's just that...

This creature looks
exactly like those things
that were chasing me
earlier.

And just now you were
reexperiencing the fear
you felt when they were
chasing you, I take it...

Do not worry. You are
safe now. Besides, they
are not even the same
species.

There's no need to
console me! I'm not
afraid... I was just...curious
about them is all!
It's nothing. I'm perfectly\nfine.

Perhaps we should
attempt to diagnose your
condition with the
scanner?
I get dizzy from time to\ntime is all. The both of you\nare overreacting.
That, my friend, is\nclassified as Rank 3\n<font color=yellow>harassment</font>!
R-Rank 3 harassment!?
Yes. Any more of this\nnonsense and you will find\nyourself in a world of pain.
Captain...I'm scared for\nyou. P-please be careful.

While I doubt it will have
any effect on our mission,
I will take note of these
findings.
Captain!!! I have something\nI must discuss with you\nimmediately!
What is it now?

Our counter-jamming
device has allowed me to
make an incredible
discovery!

I have detected a
structure that is
technologically superior to
anything this civilization is
capable of achieving.

A suspicious tower
housing advanced
technology? Could this be
where the jamming waves
are coming from?
I have no proof, but I\nstrongly suspect that is\nthe case.

At the very least,
investigating it should be
able to give us some
valuable insight into this
planet.

If we are especially lucky,
we might even obtain
items with which to repair
our damaged ship.
It is a win-win situation.\nThe future looks bright,\nmy friends!
And if only we had some\nsugar, the future would\nlook even brighter!
Sugar can wait. We must\ntake care of the tower\nfirst.

If it is as sophisticated as
you claim, there is a
possibility that the
building's guard systems
are still in place.
We must be sure to keep\nour wits about us at all\ntimes.

Welcome back! To think
that the tower is actually
a research facility of some
sort... How curious.

Yes. What's more―we
were able to obtain the
data that was left behind
by whoever was running it.
Captain, would you like me\nto begin analyzing it?

...This data format is
nothing like federation
standard. It will take some
time for me to decode.

I could not fix the sensors,
nor immediately determine
the cause of their
failure...and now I find
myself unable to read this
code...

I may as well be a hunk of
metal for all the good I am
outside federation
borders!
Perhaps, for now. But you\nwill prove your worth soon\nenough.
Yes, but...

Coro, you are the only one
of us who possesses the
tools necessary to analyze
this data.
We are relying on you to\nsee that our hard work is\nnot wasted.

Besides, aren't you always
bragging about how
persistence is your best
quality?
I do not ever recall saying\nsuch a thing...

Though, it is not to say
there is no truth to those
words! Perseverance
might as well be my
middle name!
That's the spirit! There's\nhope yet that one day you\nwill do the captain proud!
I shall do whatever it\ntakes!
E.V.E., despite everything,\ndeep down you are a good\nperson.
I certainly hope so...
You have obtained <font color=yellow>Cryptic\nData</font>.
Mayday! Mayday! We have\na crisis on our hands!

I have discovered what
might very well be the
most dangerous place in
these lands!

If Eve were to get wind of
this, she would drag you
out there in a heartbeat.
Thinking of the dangers
involved, however, such
action is not advisable...

Then again, to squander a
golden opportunity would
be most regrettable. By
the same token―
I-I am sorry. I became\noverwhelmed...
Please, have a look here.

If you continue
investigating the area you
just left, you will come
across a cave.
The locals call it the\n<font color=yellow>Man-Eating Cave</font>.

Any who dare enter are
said to be swallowed
whole, vanishing without
even the faintest trace.
...And how exactly did you\nobtain this information?
Hehehe! Thank you for\nasking!
Behold the fruits of my\nlabor! You see―
This sounds like it's going\nto take too long. Leave\nthe explanations for later.
E.V.E.! E.V.E.! E.V.E.!

A man-eating cave, huh?
That sounds like an old
wives' tale. I'm sure such
stories are common on
underdeveloped planets.

You dismiss my research
far too easily! There is
more truth to this than
you realize!

Were that cave not
possessed of some
terrifying danger, the
superstition would likely
not have arisen.

That danger could be any
number of things―poison
gas emissions, a
bottomless swamp, deadly
beasts...
Whatever it is, that tale is\ntold to simply ensure that\nno one enters the cave.
Perhaps.

The locals avoid it for a
reason. As for why, I am
sure we will find out soon
enough.

Like you say, Captain,
perhaps this place is
simply misunderstood by
the people here.

That said, there is merit
to investigating the area.
We might be able to
obtain some valuable
resources there.
I knew it would turn out\nlike this. I should never\nhave told her anything...

Whatever happens,
promise me you will be
careful! This cave may be
far more dangerous than
you anticipate!

The battle is over. The
enemies near the
entrance of the cave have
been eliminated. We are a
step closer to achieving
our goal.

You should be fine. From
what I can tell, there are
no poisonous gases inside
the cave.
So this is the man-eating\ncave...? It looks so\nunremarkable...

As unremarkable as it
may seem, you do not yet
know what dangers await
you inside. You had best
remain vigilant.
The only "dangers" here\nare the beasts we killed\nearlier.
Indeed. The real peril no\ndoubt lies within the cave.
I'm not worried. Eve is the\nscariest thing here.

Maybe... The creatures
inhabiting this area were
the same as those you
encountered at the
research facility, after all.

Do you think there is a
possibility that place and
this cave are somehow
related...?

Wait. Is it possible that
the man-eating cave
rumor was started by the
people at the facility to
keep locals away!?

...It is not an impossibility.
To know for sure,
however, you must move
forward with your
investigation.
I agree. I shall attempt to\nanalyze the cave's interior\nfor any potential hazards.
It looks like we are going\nto have to get our hands\na little dirty!

If I did not know any
better, I would say you
sound almost excited,
Eve?
Far from it!
Captain, you have just\nstepped onto a proverbial\nminefield...
Hahaha... Very funny,\n<player>.
You had best hope\nwhatever is in that cave\nkills you first.
Captain, we hit the\njackpot!

I have detected equipment
from a highly advanced
civilization from the other
side of the man-eating
cave.
That is fantastic news!\n...So why don't you sound\nmore excited?

My emotional response
unit is currently set to
low. Most of my
processing power is
allocated to analyzing your
surroundings.
You should keep it that\nway.
Sorrow detected.\nOverridden. Current\noperation prioritized.
The closer you draw, the\nstronger the jamming\nwaves will grow.
Exactly. If you shut it\ndown, the waves should\ndisappear.
Excellent! It will be but a\nsmoldering pile of metal\nonce I'm done with it!

W-wait! You must not
destroy it. You absolutely,
positively must not
destroy it!
...It sounds like your\nemotional response unit is\nback to normal.
That would be because I\nhave completed my\nanalysis.
But that is beside the\npoint!

The apparatus emitting
those waves must not be
destroyed! Are you
hearing me, Eve!?
Instead, what you must do\nis remove the energy unit\npowering the tower.
This should cause it to\nshut down and our\nproblem will be solved.

Or, if we are lucky, better
than solved―I think we
might be able to use this
energy unit to power our
own ship!
Well, aren't you a crafty\none.
Crafty!? Smart, perhaps,\nbut not crafty. I stand by\na rigid moral code!

All right, Captain. We had
best get going. Much is
riding on the success of
this mission!
By golly gosh! Y-you done\nit! You actually done it,\nCaptain!
Your excitement has\nthrown your speech\nfunctions off.
Ahem. My apologies.

I am pleased to report
that the jamming waves
have disappeared, and the
sensors are back up and
running!

Added to that, we got our
hands on the tower's
energy unit. Excellent
work, Captain!
Hmph. It is me you should\nbe thanking. I'm the one\nwho retrieved it!
Well, you may have had a\nlittle something to do with\nit. Thanks, Eve, I guess.
Huh!? Why you\nungrateful―!
Never mind. I am not going\nto let you ruin my good\nmood.

See you soon. I shall be
awaiting your return to
the ship, antennae long in
anticipation!
We are now in orbit.
Shield systems are up and\nrunning.
So you were able to use\nthe energy unit without\nissue?

Yes, it is compatible with
our ship! In fact, I have
even managed to bring
our shields up to 36
percent!

So long as we are not
attacked, we should now
be able to travel through
space safely.

Happy to hear it. ...Though,
I do wonder what that
tower was for and why it
was producing jamming
waves...
I cannot make any sense\nof it.
About that...
What?
I did not anticipate any of\nthis would happen, so I did\nnot run any numbers...

As it turns out, however, I
did stumble upon
information pertaining to
that matter in
the―ahem―federation
manual.

O-our ship services were
down and I did the very
best I could given the
resources we had! I swear!

I agree. We know that you
work hard and, while we
do not always show it, we
appreciate your efforts.
Th-thank you. Now, if I\nmay continue...
After the sensors came\nback online, I launched an\ninvestigation sequence.

I learned that, located just
below the surface of
Maere, are large mining
sites.
Exactly! Nothing gets past\nyou, Captain!

The locals simply do not
possess technology
sufficient to excavate at
such depths.

The natural conclusion
would be that another
race of people is
exploiting this planet's
resources.

It would, at the very least,
explain what the tower
emitting jamming waves
was for and why the data
we obtained is
indecipherable.
To think that someone is\nexploiting the resources of\nthis planet!
Such a wicked act can't\nbe forgiven!
It's an easy trap to fall\ninto. We must be sure we\ndo not do the same.
Is picking bananas\nconsidered "exploiting\nresources"?
I wholeheartedly agree!

I shall take note of what
we discussed. Upon our
return to the federation, I
will file an official report.

Though, this place is so
far outside federation
jurisdiction that there is
little chance it will make a
difference.

Captain, if I may, I believe
what we are doing can be
classified as "borrowing"
resources. It is a far cry
from depriving the people
of Maere of all they have!
That you, however, would\nshow such concern―you\nare truly a leader of men!

Enough! Instead of
distracting ourselves with
such trivial matters, we
must focus on the real
problem―the villains who
are siphoning this planet's
vitality!

I suppose that
depends―do you intend to
devour this planet's entire
stockpile of bananas!?

Captain, I must apologize
for being so negligent. I
was not aware that you
loved bananas so much.
Our next mission will be to
find you some!
How can the two of you\nmake light of such a grave\nsituation!?

We cannot rest until we
find the perpetrators of
this heinous crime and
bring them to justice!

The people of Maere are
being denied a very basic
right. Without access to
their own resources, how
are they to evolve as a
civilization!?

...<player>, while I do not
want to come between
you and your return
home...

We must do all in our
power to see that these
evildoers are brought to
justice!
Please, will you stand by\nme and help me right this\nwrong?
Thank you!
I cannot put into words\nhow relieved I am to hear\nthat!

And don't think I've
forgotten you, Coro! I'll be
counting on you, too. Now
let us save Maere!
...And off she goes...

Eve is a lot more excitable
than I took her to be. I am
beginning to see her in a
different light.

I have finished mapping a
route to the next star
system. Now, let us be off,
so we can assist Eve in
her crusade for justice!

During our flight, I will
analyze the data we
obtained from the
research facilities.

You have discovered a
New Route. You can now
choose this New Route
from the Select Planet
screen.
